output.summary: A small deciduous shrub native to cool temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere, it grows mainly on wet acidic soils. It has brown stems, blue-green leaves with pale net-like veins, and hanging pale-pink flowers. Its dark blue-black berries have sweet white flesh and may be eaten raw, cooked or dried.
output.edibilityNote: Berries are eaten raw or cooked, made into jelly, pies or infused liquor, and dried for pemmican.
